content_sanskrit: अथ वीर इवारक्तः कालेनास्तमितो रविः । अस्त्रतेजःपरिम्लानप्रतापोऽब्धौ समुज्झितः
padaccheda: अथ । अस्त्रतेजःपरिम्लानप्रतापः । रविः । वीरः । इव । आरक्तः । कालेन । अस्तमितः । अब्धौ । समुज्झितः
anvaya: अथ अस्त्र-तेजः-परिम्लान-प्रतापः (सः) रविः वीरः इव आरक्तः (सन्) कालेन अस्तमितः (तथा) अब्धौ समुज्झितः (अभवत्)।
meaning_english: Then the sun, like a reddened warrior whose valor had faded due to the brilliance of weapons, was set by Time and cast into the ocean.

padaccheda: सूर्यशिरश्छेदे । व्योमदर्पणप्रतिबिम्बिता । रणरक्तरुचिः । संध्यालेखा । क्षणम् । उदभूत् । जहौ
anvaya: सूर्य-शिरः-छेदे (सति) व्योम-दर्पण-प्रतिबिम्बिता रण-रक्त-रुचिः संध्या-लेखा क्षणम् उदभूत् (सा च) जहौ।
meaning_english: Upon the severing of the sun's head, the glow of evening appeared for a moment, reflected in the mirror of the sky like the hue of blood from the battlefield, and then vanished.

content_sanskrit: भूपातालनभोदिग्भ्यः प्रलयब्धिजलौघवत् । समाजग्मुस्तनत्ताला वेताला वलया इव
padaccheda: भूपातालनभोदिग्भ्यः । प्रलयब्धिजलौघवत् । वलयाः । इव । तनत्तालाः । वेतालाः । समाजग्मुः
anvaya: भू-पाताल-नभः-दिग्भ्यः प्रलय-अब्धि-जल-ओघवत् वलयाः इव नत्-तालाः वेतालाः समाजग्मुः।
meaning_english: From the earth, netherworlds, sky, and directions, vampires arrived like circling waves, clapping their hands like the surging waters of the dissolution ocean.
On the head of the great elephant of day, which was struck by the sword of polished darkness, pearls in the form of stars were scattered, reddened by the twilight glow.

content_sanskrit: निःसत्त्वेषु तमोन्धेषु रसनारसशालिषु । संकोचमाययुः पद्मामृतानां हृदयेष्विव
padaccheda: निःसत्त्वेषु । तमोन्धेषु । रसनारसशालिषु । मृतानाम् । हृदयेषु । इव । पद्मानि । संकोचम् । आययुः
anvaya: निःसत्त्वेषु तमः-अन्धेषु रसना-रस-शालिषु (सत्सु) मृतानां हृदयेषु इव पद्मानि संकोचम् आययुः।
meaning_english: When all beings became listless, blinded by darkness, and immersed in the taste of sleep, the lotuses contracted as if they were the hearts of the dead.

content_sanskrit: मीलत्पक्षाः क्षणात्सुप्ताः कृच्छ्रप्रोच्छ्रितकन्धराः । कुलायेषु खगा आसञ्छवाङ्गेष्विव हेतयः
padaccheda: कुलायेषु । खगाः । मीलत्पक्षाः । क्षणात् । सुप्ताः । कृच्छ्रप्रोच्छ्रितकन्धराः । शवाङ्गेषु । हेतयः । इव । आसन्
anvaya: कुलायेषु खगाः मीलत्-पक्षाः क्षणात् सुप्ताः कृच्छ्र-प्रोच्छ्रित-कन्धराः (सन्तः) शव-अङ्गेषु हेतयः इव आसन्।
meaning_english: In their nests, the birds with closed wings fell asleep instantly with their necks slightly raised, appearing like weapons lodged in the limbs of corpses.

content_sanskrit: आसन्नचन्द्रसुभगा लोकाः कुसुमपङ्क्तयः । उल्लसद्धृदया जाता वीरपक्षेष्विव श्रियः
padaccheda: आसन्नचन्द्रसुभगाः । लोकाः । कुसुमपङ्क्तयः । वीरपक्षेषु । श्रियः । इव । उल्लसद्धृदयाः । जाताः
anvaya: आसन्न-चन्द्र-सुभगाः लोकाः कुसुम-पङ्क्तयः (च) वीर-पक्षेषु श्रियः इव उल्लसत्-हृदयाः जाताः।
meaning_english: With the lovely moon approaching, the worlds and the rows of flowers became joyful at heart, like the fortunes favoring the side of the brave warriors.

padaccheda: सायम् । रणभूमिः । इव । अब्जिनी । रक्तवारिमयी । अङ्गगुप्तशिलीमुखा । संकुचद्वक्त्रपद्मा । अभूत्
anvaya: सायं रण-भूमिः इव अब्जिनी रक्त-वारि-मयी अङ्ग-गुप्त-शिली-मुखा संकुचत्-वक्त्र-पद्मा अभूत्।
meaning_english: In the evening, the lotus-pond became like a battlefield; it was filled with blood-red water, its bees were hidden within like arrows in bodies, and its lotus-faces were closing.

padaccheda: उपरि । ताराकुमुदमण्डितम् । व्योमसरः । अभूत् । अधः । तु । स्फुरत्कुमुदतारकम् । वारिसरः । अभूत्
anvaya: उपरि तारा-कुमुद-मण्डितं व्योम-सरः अभूत् अधः तु स्फुरत्-कुमुद-तारकं वारि-सरः अभूत्।
meaning_english: Above, the lake of the sky was adorned with stars as its lilies; below, the lake of water was filled with lilies appearing as stars.

content_sanskrit: तमस्यपेतभीतानि भूतानि मिलितान्यलम् । पयांसीव विसेतूनि प्रसृतानि दिशं प्रति
padaccheda: तमसि । अपेतभीतानि । भूतानि । विसेतूनि । पयांसि । इव । अलम् । मिलितानि । दिशम् । प्रति । प्रसृतानि
anvaya: तमसि अपेत-भीतानि भूतानि वि-सेतूनि पयांसि इव अलम् मिलितानि (सन्ति) दिशं प्रति प्रसृतानि।
meaning_english: In the darkness, beings whose fear had vanished gathered together and spread out toward every direction, like waters breaking through their embankments.
The battlefield was crowded with singing groups of vetālas (ghosts), and it was the playground for herons and crows perched on creaking skeletons.
Then, the battlefield shone like the starry sky with the flames of wooden funeral pyres, where fires of fat and flesh burned with a crackling 'pacha-pacha' sound.
Rising towards the sky were heaps of pyres bursting with the loud cracking of bones from all limbs, partially hidden by the water-play initiated by female vetālas.

anvaya: श्व-काक-यक्ष-वेताल-ताल-कोलाहल-उल्बणम् भूतानाम् गम-आगमेन समुड्डीन-वन-उपमम् (तत् रणाङ्गणं बभूव)।
meaning_english: Intense with the tumultuous noise and rhythm of dogs, crows, yakṣas, and vetālas, it resembled a forest where all creatures were fleeing in constant movement.
Ḍākinīs were preoccupied with snatching blood, flesh, marrow, and fat, while piśācas had blood, fat, and flesh dripping from the corners of their mouths as they chewed.
Heaps of bloody corpses were made visible by the light of pyres scattered here and there, while female ghouls (virūpikās) carried large corpses positioned upon their shoulders.
The center was terrifying with circles of kumbhāṇḍas performing wild dances; it echoed with 'chamicchamit' sounds and was filled with clouds of vapor from fat and blood.
Earth-dwelling spirits were swept away by the force of flowing rivers of blood, while the air was filled with the low, confused cries of vetālas dragging skeletons.
Young vetālas slept within the chests of dead elephants as if in boxes, and rākṣasas stood in solitary parts of the battlefield engaged in drinking games.
The field blazed with the clash of firebrands from pyres used in the fights of intoxicated vetālas, while the wind was thick with the heavy scent of flowing blood and fat.

The battlefield echoed with the harsh, rattling screams of a multitude of female ghouls (rūpikā). It was filled with the exuberant strife of Yakṣas, who were greedy to taste the half-cooked flesh of the corpses.

Birds of prey swarmed over the fallen bodies of soldiers from Tuṅga, Vaṅga, Kaliṅga, Aṅga, Taṅgaṇa, and Aṅgala. The Rūpikās appeared with flames leaping from their mouths, outshining the brilliance of falling stars.
Vampires (Vetālas) leapt joyfully amidst falling bodies, their forms made hideous by smeared blood. Nearby, the leaders of the Yoginī clans were being listened to by attentive Piśācas.

Musical sounds were produced as if on great lutes using the long, stretched-out entrails of the dead. Mortals, driven by the morbid impressions of Piśācas as they died, were being transformed into ghosts themselves.

Noble warriors lay half-dead, paralyzed by the unprecedented terror of beholding the Rūpikās. In some places, the Madraka soldiers were being devoured, though not yet fully consumed, by Vetālas and Rakṣasas.

Even the night-roaming demons (Niśācaras) were startled as corpses fell onto the shoulders of the Rūpikās. The sky became congested and turbulent as unprecedented throngs of spirits collided with one another.
Flesh was snatched with great effort from men who were still in the throes of death. Heaps of corpses were tossed about like discarded scraps among factions competing for their own share of food.
With the red gore rising like sparks from the flames of jackals' mouths, the battlefield appeared as if clusters of fresh Aśoka flowers were flying up on all sides.
Young Vetālas were busy clinging to the headless necks of trunks. The sky was lit up by flaming torches carried by Yakṣas, Rakṣasas, and Piśācas moving through the air.

The battlefield was filled with masses of darkness like clouds, adorning the caves and thickets of the celestial mountains. It resembled a small collection of cosmic eggs being tossed by the Kalpa winds, agitated by the violent speed of wandering ghosts.
